title: The constant coefficient objects are bounded constructible
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and for $n\geq1$ put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Y$ be a scheme, with small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; let $(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the constant sheaf of the ring $A_{E,n}$ on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (the sheafification of the constant presheaf, as in that definition), and let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Then:

1. $(A_{E,n})_Y$, placed in degree $0$, is an object of $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]: it is locally constant on the single stratum $Y$ with finite stalks $A_{E,n}$.
2. $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, placed in degree $0$, is an object of $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: it is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], the canonical map $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\to(A_{E,n})_Y$ (the derived reduction modulo $\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]) is an isomorphism for every $n\geq1$, and the cohomological supports [def-weil-cohomological-support] of these reductions are all contained in $[0,0]$.
3. Consequently $E_Y$, the image of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$ in the rationalized category $D^b_c(Y,E)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $(\Qlb)_Y=(E,E_Y)$ in the common-stage category $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], are objects of those categories, and $(\Qlb)_Y$ is independent of the stage $E$: for finite extensions $E\subset L$ in $\Qlb$, the integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] gives an isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$, hence $E_Y\otimes_EL\cong L_Y$ in $D^b_c(Y,L)$, and its class is an isomorphism $(E,E_Y)\cong(L,L_Y)$ in $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$.

source.place: node def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology, order 1510: 'let $\Lambda_Y$ denote its coefficient object on the small pro-etale site ... Abbreviate $H^i(Y,\Lambda)=H^i(Y,\Lambda_Y)$' (for $H^i(Y,\Lambda_Y)$ to be defined, $\Lambda_Y$ must be an object of $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$; the blueprint does not say so). The integral case is Bhatt-Scholze, literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Definition 6.8.1 and Lemma 6.8.2(1) ($\mathcal O_{E,X}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_E=\varprojlim_n\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$)

proof.text: By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $A_{E,n}$ is finite. Stratify $Y$ by $Y$ itself: it is open and retrocompact in $Y$, hence locally closed and constructible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and the constant sheaf is locally constant using the identity cover [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Its stalks at geometric points [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] are $A_{E,n}$ by [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk]. Its degree-zero complex has only $\mathcal H^0=(A_{E,n})_Y$; all other cohomology vanishes. Thus [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] gives Part 1 and [def-weil-cohomological-support] gives support in $[0,0]$. This includes empty $Y$.

source.place: §6.5, Definition 6.5.1, p. 49; finite constant sheaf specialization

proof.text: Write $R_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. Apply [lem-weil-constant-scalar-strict-unit] with $L=E$. Its K-flat regular representative and multiplication maps give the canonical isomorphisms $R_E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong(A_{E,n})_Y$; their transition maps and reduction units are precisely the quotient transitions and limit projections. Step 1 supplies constructibility and the uniform interval $[0,0]$ for every reduction.

For $L=E$, [lem-weil-constant-scalar-unit-quasi-isomorphism] supplies a distinguished Roos triangle with first map the prescribed reduction units. This is derived completeness in [def-weil-derived-complete]. Together with Steps 1-2 it verifies every condition of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], proving Part 2.

Rationalization has the same objects as the integral category, so Part 2 gives $E_Y\in D^b_c(Y,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. The pair $(E,E_Y)$ is then an object of $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$ by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

source.place: Definition 6.8.1 and Lemma 6.8.2(2), pp. 58-59; DAG rationalization and pair definitions

proof.text: For $E\subset L$, [lem-weil-constant-scalar-unit-quasi-isomorphism] identifies the strict cone defining integral scalar extension with $R_L$, giving $R_E\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong R_L$. Part 2 for $L$ puts both objects in the full integral constructible category. Rationalize to obtain $\phi:E_Y\otimes_EL\cong L_Y$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; the same construction for $E=L$ gives $\psi:L_Y\otimes_LL\cong L_Y$. Over common stage $L$, $u=\psi^{-1}\phi$ and $u^{-1}$ represent inverse morphisms between $(E,E_Y)$ and $(L,L_Y)$: their composites are identities over $L$, hence identity classes by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. This proves Part 3.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1)-(2), pp. 58-59; scalar cone and common-stage assembly are agent-written
